lesson_title: Surface Area, Volume and Capacity of Cubes and Prisms
hook_text: A juice carton labelled 250 ml. She measured it — and it holds more.
clip_script:
At the camp, a learner looks at a juice carton labelled 250 millilitres. It measures 4 centimetres by 6,3 centimetres by 10 centimetres. Length times breadth times height: 252 cubic centimetres — and every cubic centimetre holds exactly one millilitre.

So the carton holds 252 millilitres, a little more than the label, leaving an air gap so it opens without spilling. The card wrapping it is a different measure: six faces, about 256 square centimetres. Inside, cubic units and millilitres; outside, square units. Same box, two questions.
visual_style: A juice carton unfolds into its net with face areas labelled, then refolds and fills with tiny centimetre cubes that pour out as millilitres
call_to_action: Open the full session to measure the outside and the inside of any prism.
